Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala addressing the inaugural function of ‘Sibaq’ national arts festival of Darul Huda Islamic University at Chemmad in Malappuram on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: SAKEER HUSSAIN
India cannot be imagined by excluding its 25 crore Muslims, and the right to vote is a fundamental right of every citizen in a democracy, Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has said.
He accused the BJP government at the Centre of using the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls to exclude minorities.
Mr. Chennithala was speaking at the inaugural of Darul Huda Islamic University’s national arts festival named ‘Sibaq’ at Chemmad near Tirurangadi on Tuesday night.
M.P. Abdussamad Samadani, MP, (left) looks towards fellow MP Imran Pratapgarhi while translating his Urdu speech at Darul Huda Islamic University’s national arts festival ‘Sibaq’ at Chemmad in Malappuram on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: SAKEER HUSSAIN
Syed Rasheedali Shihab Thangal inaugurated the festival. Darul Huda Vice-Chancellor Bahaudheen Mohammed Nadwi presided over the function.
Delivering the keynote address, All India Congress Committee Minority department chairman Imran Pratapgarhi, MP, said festivals such as Sibaq helped young people become voices for a better future in a pluralistic India.
Around 4,000 students from 20 States, representing 40 Darul Huda campuses, are taking part in the festival, which will conclude on November 29. Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan will be the chief guest at the university’s convocation ceremony on the concluding day.
